primary_claim: Shift-by-k-months function vectors extracted from low-diversity few-shot prompts (Llama-3.2-3B) pass all three classic validation checks (behavioral gate, stability, causal effect) yet encode a completely different task (outputting an adjacent month, ignoring k), with margin scores as low as -1.000 in the most extreme case, and lower example diversity simultaneously makes the checks look better (few-shot accuracy 0.38 to 0.83) while making the vector's true identity worse

effect.metric: margin (correct shift-by-k occurrences minus neighbor-task occurrences, among cases where they differ) across month-diversity sets
effect.value: margin +0.35 (12 months) and +0.34 (9 months) down to -0.31, -0.46, -0.70, -0.94 (6- and 4-month range sets), with -1.000 for the September-December subset; behavioral gate rises from 0.38 to 0.83 as diversity drops

contradicts_or_qualifies: shows that the standard function-vector validation checks used in prior work (Todd et al.'s behavioral gate and causal effect, Hendel et al.'s reliability-style check) can all pass while the vector's actual encoded function differs from the intended one -- a distinct failure mode from the known 'steering vectors that fail to steer' (Tan et al.) or 'intervention illusion' (Makelov et al.) findings

the 12 extracted shift vectors did not trace a circle in activation space regardless of extraction method, differing from prior findings of circular representations for months/days/emotions (Engels et al., Modell et al., Sun et al.), consistent instead with Karkada et al.'s theory that circularity stems from training-data symmetries which shift-by-k operations lack
stated_future_work: run the same diversity test on another classic task family with a limited answer set to see whether the diversity phenomenon generalizes (registered as next experiment T7)
limitations_stated: measured on a single model, a single circular task family (month shifts), and mainly one extraction method (Todd's); the Hendel method produced no vector performing the intended task so it could not be compared
threshold calibration is sensitive to method choice: random-data thresholds were 145-156x too low or up to 100x too high compared to thresholds from shuffled real vectors
quote: The culprit is the number of distinct example inputs. Lower diversity makes the model perform the few-shot task better (from 0.38 to 0.83) even though the function vector changes identity, so the checks actually favor the imposters.
